An emergency license is a one-year nonrenewable license, and it is valid only until June 30 of the fiscal year for which it was requested, so any license granted last year has already expired or will expire on June 30 and cannot be renewed.

A teacher license requires completion of an educator preparation program at the bachelor's, master's, specialist, or doctoral level, except that applicants with only a high school diploma or associate's degree may be issued a teaching license only in Career and Technical Education, JROTC, or Safety and Driver Education.

A CPL must be renewed every five years, and a teacher renewing it must complete eight CEUs in the renewal cycle, with the composition depending on grade band; one CEU equals either two-thirds of a semester credit hour or ten clock hours of professional development.

A teacher employed by a local board must also have a rating of at least Proficient on three of five NC Professional Teaching Standards, including Standard 4, on the most recent annual evaluation to renew a CPL.

If a teacher employed by a local board is in the final year of a renewal cycle and was not deemed proficient, the LSAU may place the teacher on a mandatory improvement plan, which results in an IPL if the teacher otherwise meets requirements. If no plan is placed and the teacher meets Section 1 criteria, the license expires at the end of the renewal cycle, and the teacher may apply for an IPL 30 days after notice of expiration.

A PSU governing body may request validation of an expired CPL even without the requisite CEUs, provided the educator was not employed by any PSU during the preceding fiscal year. A validated CPL is effective for three years, and the educator must then complete renewal requirements by the end of the third year to renew for a new five-year cycle.

An IPL is a three-year nonrenewable license for an applicant who has completed a recognized NC EPP and been recommended, or who has completed an out-of-state EPP, or who holds a clear out-of-state license with fewer than three years of licensed teaching experience there.
A limited license requires that the applicant has met G.S. 115C-270.20(a)(4a) and it is for teaching license areas only; its renewal depends on employment and EVAAS growth.

Because of that rule, a permit to teach holder cannot receive experience credit or graduate degree pay on the basis of education or prior work experience, while an emergency license holder may be eligible for those under LICN-006.
Experience credit under LICN-006 §I is earned by full-time work in a school unit of at least six calendar months within a fiscal year, which earns one year of experience credit.

Non-teaching work experience can count toward experience credit only if it is relevant, at least half-time (20 hours or more per week), completed after age 18, not on-the-job training, and paid and documented, and it requires the recommendation of the employing LEA's personnel administrator.

Graduate degree pay under LICN-006 §V requires the degree to be from an accredited institution, directly related to the license area or assignment, and tied to a majority (50% or more) of the school day assignment, among other criteria.

An emergency license requires a bachelor's degree with at least 18 credit hours of relevant coursework, no completed recognized educator preparation program in that area, and that the applicant does not qualify for a residency license.

Both an emergency license and a permit to teach are valid until June 30 of the fiscal year for which they were requested and cannot be extended or renewed.
A person who holds or previously held a residency license is not eligible for a permit to teach or an emergency license in the same license area.
The Department of Public Instruction cannot add add-on teaching areas to either a permit to teach or an emergency license.

question: Is there a Limited License for teachers, and when is it used?

input.query: Is there a Limited License for teachers, and when is it used?

answer.summary: Yes. A Limited License is one of the teacher license classifications, and it is a three-year renewable license for a teaching license area. It is generally used when an employed teacher has completed preparation but has not yet passed the required licensure exam, with the most specific pathway in the passages being a former lateral entry license holder who is currently employed by the public school unit (PSU) and meets the other conditions.

claims.text: A Limited License is one of the teacher license classifications listed in the teacher license policy, with its qualifications set out in the Limited License policy.

A Limited License means a three-year renewable license issued to an individual who has completed an educator preparation program (EPP) but has not satisfied the applicable licensure examination requirements.

The governing body of a public school unit may request a Limited License for an applicant under its employment if the applicant meets the requirements of G.S. 115C-270.20(a)(4a). A Limited License may only be issued for teaching license areas, not for administrator or student services personnel license areas.

A person who previously held a lateral entry license issued under G.S. 115C-297 (repealed by S.L. 2017-189), and who meets all requirements for an Initial Professional License (IPL) or Continuing Professional License (CPL) except passing the licensure examination for that license area, qualifies for a Limited License if the person is currently employed by the PSU governing body and the PSU submits a qualifying affidavit to DPI.

The affidavit must be signed by the local superintendent (or equivalent chief executive officer) and the applicant's school principal. It must state that the person is currently employed by the PSU, is an effective teacher, and that the PSU will encourage the applicant to pursue an IPL or CPL.

To renew a Limited License, the employing PSU must submit an affidavit attesting that the licensee is currently employed, is an effective teacher, and will be encouraged to pursue a CPL. The licensee must also meet or exceed expected growth as measured by EVAAS where data is available.

For EVAAS growth, if more than one year of data exists, DPI takes the average. Data is limited to years since the Limited License was first issued or its most recent renewal, and DPI does not consider 2019-2020 or 2020-2021 EVAAS data.
A Limited License may not be transferred from one PSU to another, except for military service members and spouses covered by LICN-028.
Limited Licenses cannot have additional teaching areas added to them.
Every license expires on June 30 of the year it is set to expire unless it is renewed, extended, or converted to another license type under SBE policy.

question: How long is a Residency License valid and can it be extended?

input.query: How long is a Residency License valid and can it be extended?
residency license valid three years term expiration

answer.summary: A Residency License is a one-year license that can be renewed twice, so it can run up to three years. Each renewal depends on the employing unit documenting that the applicant meets the renewal conditions, and the license expires if it is not renewed.

claims.text: A residency license is a one-year license, renewable twice, issued to an individual who meets the qualifications of LICN-019.

Renewal requires the employing public school unit or eligible nonpublic school to document that the applicant is enrolled in a recognized educator preparation program, is employed as a teacher there, acquired at least six months of teaching experience during the preceding school year, and, for the first-year renewal, completed 10 days of professional development.

If an applicant fails to renew a residency license for the second or third year, the license expires. The employing unit may request reinstatement if it hires the applicant within three years of the initial residency license's effective date, provided the license has not already been renewed twice and the applicant is enrolled in a recognized educator preparation program.

To convert a residency license to an Initial Professional License or Continuing Professional License, the applicant must meet the requirements for that license and be recommended by the educator preparation program that prepared them. If the applicant meets those requirements by June 30 of the third year, the new license is effective July 1 of the next fiscal year; otherwise the residency license expires and the new license is effective when the requirements are met.

The policies use the terms "renewable" and "renew" for residency licenses. They do not describe a separate "extension" for residency licenses. Permits to teach and emergency licenses are the ones the policies say cannot be extended or renewed.

If a servicemember or spouse pursuing a residency license is called to active duty or relocated outside North Carolina by military orders, the three-year timeframe is held in abeyance until they return to North Carolina and employment in a North Carolina public school.

question: What are the requirements for a CPL in terms of years of experience and renewal cycle?

input.query: What are the requirements for a CPL in terms of years of experience and renewal cycle?
years of experience required for continuing professional administrator or student services personnel license

answer.summary: A continuing professional license (CPL) is a five-year renewable license. For teachers, the CPL requires an initial professional or residency license plus at least three years of licensed teaching experience, and renewal requires 8 CEUs each five-year cycle. The passages set no fixed years-of-experience minimum for administrator or student services personnel CPLs; those depend on other policies (LICN-011 and LICN-012) that were not provided.

claims.text: A CPL is a five-year, renewable license issued to an applicant or professional educator who meets the relevant requirements established by SBE policy.

To qualify for a continuing professional teacher license, an applicant must hold an initial professional educator license or residency license in North Carolina, and have at least three years of licensed teaching experience.
A teacher's CPL must be renewed every five years.

Teachers in Pre-K through Grade 5 must complete eight CEUs per renewal cycle: three in the license area, three related to literacy, and two general CEUs germane to the K-12 environment. Teachers in Grades 6 through 12 must complete eight CEUs: four in the license area and four general CEUs.

Teachers employed by a local board of education must have a rating of at least proficient on their most recent annual evaluation to renew a CPL, defined as Proficient or higher on three of the five NC Professional Teaching Standards including Proficient on Standard 4.

For an administrator or student services personnel CPL, the applicant must satisfy licensure examination requirements before or during the third year of licensure and meet the other requirements of LICN-011 or LICN-012. The passages do not state a years-of-experience minimum for these CPLs.

Administrator licenses must be renewed every five years with eight CEUs per cycle: four focused on instruction, human resources, and management leadership, and four general CEUs germane to the K-12 environment.

Student services personnel licenses must be renewed every five years with eight CEUs per cycle: four aligned with the NC standards for the professional discipline under EVAL, and four general CEUs germane to the K-12 environment.

An out-of-state applicant with more than three years of licensed professional educator experience may qualify for a CPL if they meet the clear-license and substantially-similar (or National Board certification) criteria.

If a teacher, what grade band do they teach (Pre-K to 5 or 6 to 12)? This sets the CEU breakdown.

answer.summary: To convert a residency license (RL) to an IPL, the applicant must meet the IPL requirements in LICN-020 and be recommended by the educator preparation program (EPP) that prepared them. If those requirements are met by June 30 of the RL's third year, the IPL takes effect July 1 of the next fiscal year; if not, the RL expires and the IPL takes effect when the requirements are met.

claims.text: To convert a residency license to an IPL or CPL, the applicant must meet the requirements for an IPL in LICN-020 (or a CPL in LICN-024) and must be recommended by the EPP that prepared the licensee.

LICN-020 requires either completion of a recognized North Carolina EPP with EPP recommendation for the requested license, completion of an EPP based outside North Carolina, or a clear out-of-state license with fewer than three years of licensed teaching experience in that jurisdiction.

Timing: if the applicant satisfies the requirements by June 30 of the third year of the residency license, the IPL or CPL is effective July 1 of the next fiscal year. If not, the residency license expires and the IPL or CPL is effective on the date the applicant satisfies the requirements.

To keep the residency license in force, the employing PSU or eligible nonpublic school must document each year that the applicant is enrolled in a recognized EPP, is employed as a teacher there, and acquired at least six months of teaching experience in the preceding school year. In the first year, the applicant must also have completed 10 days of professional development.

If the applicant fails to renew the residency license for the second or third year, the license expires. The hiring PSU or nonpublic school may request reinstatement within three years of the initial residency license's effective date, provided the license has not already been renewed twice and the applicant is employed and enrolled in a recognized EPP.

LICN-020 §2 allows a PSU to request an IPL for an applicant who has completed all academic, field, clinical, and other requirements for a recognized North Carolina EPP but has not satisfied the licensure examination requirements, and in that case EPP recommendation is not required. This sits in tension with LICN-019 §3(a)(ii), which requires EPP recommendation for conversion, and the passages do not resolve the conflict.

Application requirements apply to any professional educator license application, including the educational credentials, disclosures, and documentation of licensure examination performance, and the applicant must pay the application fee defined in LICN-008.

question: How many CEUs are needed to renew a CPL, and do any have to be in a specific area?

input.query: How many CEUs are needed to renew a CPL, and do any have to be in a specific area?

answer.summary: The CEU requirement depends on the educator's role and, for teachers, grade band: teachers need 8 CEUs per five-year cycle, administrators need 8, and student services personnel need 8, with some portion of each set to a specific area. Please confirm the educator's role and grade band before giving a final answer.

claims.text: A CPL must be renewed every five years, and teachers, administrators, and student services personnel each must complete eight CEUs in each renewal cycle.

For teachers in Pre-Kindergarten through Grade 5, the 8 CEUs are 3 in the teacher's license area (Standards 3 and 4), 3 related to literacy, and 2 general CEUs germane to the K-12 environment. Here 3 + 3 + 2 = 8. Two of the three categories are area-specific (license area and literacy).

For teachers in Grades 6 through 12, the 8 CEUs are 4 in the teacher's license area (Standards 3 and 4) and 4 general CEUs germane to the K-12 environment. Here 4 + 4 = 8. Four must be in the license area.

For administrators, the 8 CEUs are 4 focused on the administrator's leadership role in instruction, human resources, and management, and 4 general CEUs germane to the K-12 environment. Here 4 + 4 = 8. Four must be leadership-focused.

For student services personnel, the 8 CEUs are 4 that align with the North Carolina standards for the relevant professional discipline under the EVAL policy series, and 4 general CEUs germane to the K-12 environment. Here 4 + 4 = 8. Four must align with the discipline standards.
A school audiologist or school speech-language pathologist is exempt from these continuing education requirements as long as they continue to meet the applicable LICN-012 requirements.
A member of the General Assembly is exempt from the teacher continuing education requirements for any renewal cycle in which they serve, if they notify DPI of the exemption during that cycle.

A CEU is either two-thirds of a semester credit hour from an institution of higher education, or ten clock hours of professional development programming. So 8 CEUs equal 5 1/3 semester credit hours (8 x 2/3) or 80 clock hours (8 x 10).

An educator who receives National Board for Professional Teaching Standards certification gets credit for all 8 CEUs for the renewal cycle in which it is received. Renewing National Board certification earns 2 CEUs for that cycle.

Mandatory training hours count toward CEUs only if the training is required by State law or by the local board as a condition of employment, and the educator has otherwise met the renewal requirements for the license type.

questions_for_user: What is the educator's role: teacher, administrator, or student services personnel? The CEU requirements differ by role.
If a teacher, what grade band do they teach: Pre-Kindergarten through Grade 5, or Grades 6 through 12?
If student services personnel, are they a school audiologist or school speech-language pathologist (which is exempt)?
Does the educator hold National Board certification, or is a renewal of it pending in this cycle?
Is the educator a member of the General Assembly who has filed an exemption notice with DPI?
Do any CEUs already earned come from mandatory training required by State law or by the local board as a condition of employment?

The policies provided do not define 'license area' for teachers or 'leadership role' in detail, nor list which courses qualify for each area-specific CEU category.
The content of the North Carolina Professional Teaching Standards and the EVAL standards referenced for area-specific CEUs is not included in the passages.
The policies provided do not state the effective dates or rules that applied to renewal cycles before 2026-07-01, so earlier requirements cannot be confirmed.

metrics.judge_rationale: The answer gives the correct eight-CEU totals, role and grade-band breakdowns, and area-specific categories, all supported by the cited policy text, and it correctly asks for role and grade band. It does not address the question's false premise that a digital learning requirement exists, which the key says must be corrected.

question: What's the renewal deadline for a standard CPL, and what happens if it lapses?

input.query: What's the renewal deadline for a standard CPL, and what happens if it lapses?
expired continuing professional license lapse reinstatement after expiration

answer.summary: A continuing professional license (CPL) is a five-year license, and under the policies provided a teacher must renew it every five years. The policies do not give a specific calendar renewal date; they say a license expires June 30 of its expiration year unless renewed. If a teacher's CPL is not renewed, it expires, and for a teacher employed by a local school administrative unit who is not deemed proficient, the outcome depends on whether the LSAU places the teacher on a mandatory improvement plan.

claims.text: A CPL is a five-year, renewable license issued to an applicant or professional educator who meets the relevant SBE requirements.
A renewal cycle is the five-year period between each renewal of a CPL.
Each teacher holding a CPL must renew that license every five years.
Every license expires on June 30 of the calendar year in which it is set to expire, unless it is renewed, extended, or converted to another type of license under SBE policy.
The April 15 submission deadline for license applications does not apply to license renewal, so the policies provided give no April 15 renewal deadline.

For a teacher employed by a local board of education, renewal requires evidence of a rating of at least Proficient on the most recent annual evaluation, meaning Proficient or higher on three of the five Professional Teaching Standards including Proficient on Standard 4.

If a teacher employed by an LSAU holds a current CPL, is in the final year of a renewal cycle, and was not deemed proficient, the LSAU may place the teacher on a mandatory improvement plan so the teacher can renew; if placed and otherwise qualified, DPI issues an IPL.

If a teacher meets the renewal criteria but is not placed on a mandatory improvement plan by the employing LSAU, the teacher's license expires at the end of the renewal cycle, and the teacher may apply for an IPL 30 days after receiving notice of expiration from DPI.

A PSU governing body may request that DPI validate an expired CPL, even without the required CEUs, if the educator was not employed by any PSU during the preceding fiscal year; a validated CPL is effective for three years, and the educator must complete the renewal requirements by the end of the third year to renew for a new five-year cycle.
Reverting from a CPL to an IPL is not a demotion and does not reduce salary.

question: What are the testing requirements for adding a licensure area?

input.query: What are the testing requirements for adding a licensure area?

answer.summary: Under LICN-013, you can add a teaching area to an IPL or CPL either by meeting the licensure exam requirement for that area or by completing 24 credit hours of higher-education coursework in the area with a C or better in each course. Elementary Education and Exceptional Children: General Curriculum can be added only by passing the exam, and several license types cannot add areas at all. The exam and score for each area are listed in LICN-003 §5.

claims.text: An applicant may request to add a new license area to an existing IPL or CPL.
An applicant may add a license area to an IPL only if the applicant has already met the licensure examination requirements for the initial license area.

To add an area to a teaching license, the applicant must either satisfy the applicable licensure examination requirements for that area, or complete 24 credit hours of coursework from an institution of higher education in that area and earn a grade of C or better in each course.
For Elementary Education and Exceptional Children: General Curriculum, the area can be added only by satisfying the licensure examination requirements. Coursework alone is not allowed.

The Department of Public Instruction will not add teaching areas under Section 1 to a Permit to Teach, Emergency License, Residency License, Limited License, Provisional License, International Faculty License, or Career and Technical Education – Restricted License.

The required exam and minimum score for each area are listed in the NCSBE-approved testing table. For example, Speech Communication requires Praxis 5221 with a score of 143, and Spanish requires Praxis 5195 (168) or the ACTFL OPI & WPT at Advanced Low.

For Academically or Intellectually Gifted, no test is required if the license was earned through a recognized Educator Preparation Program. Otherwise the area can be added by passing Praxis Gifted Education 5358 with a minimum score of 157.

An out-of-state applicant may add a teaching area based solely on a passing score on an out-of-state exam in that area, but only if the exam evidence is submitted with the initial North Carolina application. If the area is added after the NC license is issued, LICN-013 applies.

For a teacher whose license expired at the end of a renewal cycle without a mandatory improvement plan, the teacher may apply for an IPL 30 days after receiving notice of expiration from DPI.

Except for applicants with a high school diploma or associate's degree in the listed areas (Career and Technical Education, JROTC, Safety and Driver Education), an applicant must have completed an educator preparation program at the Bachelor's (A), Master's (M), Specialist (S), or Doctoral (D) level to qualify for a teacher license, and is only eligible for a license at the highest degree level at which the EPP was completed.

Each teacher license is classified as an Initial Professional License (LICN-020), Continuing Professional License (LICN-024), Residency License (LICN-019), Limited License (LICN-023), Permit to Teach (LICN-017), Emergency License (LICN-018), International Faculty License (LICN-026), Lifetime License (LICN-027), or Provisional License (LICN-014), based on the applicant's qualifications.

An IPL can be obtained by completing a recognized NC EPP and being recommended by it, by completing an EPP based outside NC, or by holding a clear out-of-state license and having fewer than three years of licensed teaching experience in that jurisdiction. An IPL allows practice as an independent professional educator in NC.

A Limited License may be issued for teaching license areas (not administrator or student services areas) to an applicant the employing PSU requests it for under G.S. 115C-270.20(a)(4a). It is a three-year renewable license and cannot be transferred between PSUs.

To move from an IPL to a CPL, the applicant must hold an NC IPL or residency license, satisfy licensure examination requirements before or during the third year of licensure, have at least three years of licensed teaching experience, and complete a Beginning Teacher Support Program unless exempt (for example, three years of licensed teaching experience outside NC).

Examination requirements for EC areas vary by area. For example, Exceptional Children General Curriculum (code 88091) requires Foundational Knowledge Test 5355 (score 145) or Pearson Test 890 Foundations of Reading (score 233), plus a mathematics subtest, while Behaviorally/Emotionally Disabled (88085) requires tests 5372 and 5511.
Exceptional Children: General Curriculum cannot be added to a license through coursework alone; it can only be added by satisfying the applicable licensure examination requirements.

The residency license for teachers requires the employing PSU to provide the teacher field experience (at least 3 hours before teaching and 10 hours over the first year) and 10 days of professional development during the first year.

An applicant is only eligible for an administrator license at the highest degree level at which the applicant completed an EPP or APP.

Any person employed as an assistant principal in a PSU must hold either a principal license or a provisional assistant principal license issued under LICN-014, Section 7.
A provisional assistant principal license is a one-year license, renewable twice, issued to an individual employed as an assistant principal who meets the requirements of LICN-014, Section 7.

Under LICN-001 §3(d), any license requiring completion of an educator preparation program requires that the EPP be recognized by the SBE or the equivalent licensing authority of the jurisdiction where it is based.

Each teacher license is classified as one of several types (Initial Professional, Continuing Professional, Residency, Limited, Permit to Teach, Emergency, International Faculty, Lifetime, or Provisional), and the applicable classification depends on the applicant's qualifications under the corresponding rule.

Career and Technical Education is a recognized teacher license classification, with areas including Agriculture Education, Aviation Education, Business/Finance/IT Education, Computer Science and IT Education, Family and Consumer Sciences (several strands), Health Sciences Education, Marketing Education, Technology/Engineering/Design Education, and multiple Trade and Industrial Education strands.

Under LICN-003 §5, the licensure test table lists these CTE areas with required Praxis tests and minimum scores: Family & Consumer Sciences (code 710, Praxis 5123, score 151); Marketing Education (730, 5561, 156); Technology Education (820, 5053, 157); Business Education (760, 5101, 154); and Computer Science & IT Education (765, 5652, 149).

Under LICN-001 §3(a), any person employed as a professional educator in a North Carolina public school must hold, or be qualified to hold, a professional educator license issued by DPI under SBE policy.

Under LICN-001 §3(d), a license that requires completion of an educator preparation program requires that the EPP be recognized by the SBE or by the equivalent licensing authority where the EPP is based.

Under LICN-004 §1, a license application must include, among other items, educational credentials, a disclosure of prior license actions and criminal history, and documentation of performance on any applicable licensure examination requirements.

For salary purposes under LICN-006 §II, non-teaching work experience may be credited toward total licensure experience if it is directly related to the area of licensure. For Class V Career-Technical Trade and Industry Education licenses, one year of credit is awarded for each year of full-time relevant experience after completing the required training and work experience for the provisional license. question: Is there a special pathway for international teachers to get an NC license?
context_ids: LICN-008 (North Carolina Department of Public Instruction Licensure Fees)

input.query: Is there a special pathway for international teachers to get an NC license?
international preparation program out-of-state applicant license requirements

answer.summary: Yes, for one group: an international faculty license exists for foreign nationals on a J-1 visa who don't qualify for any other DPI license and have a DPI-approved sponsor. Whether an international teacher can use this pathway depends on visa status, sponsor approval, and whether they qualify for another license, which the analyst needs to confirm.

claims.text: The international faculty license is available to a foreign national who does not meet the requirements for any other DPI license.

To qualify, the applicant must hold a J-1 cultural exchange visa issued by the U.S. Department of State and be supported by a sponsor, as defined in 22 C.F.R. 62.2, that DPI has approved under G.S. 115C-105.25(5a).
The license is issued only at the request of the applicant's sponsor.
The license cannot be renewed. It may be extended for two years at the request of the sponsor and the employing public school unit, provided the applicant still holds an active J-1 visa.

For State Salary Schedule pay, the license is set at the A-Level (bachelor's degree, zero years of experience) regardless of the applicant's education or prior experience. Years taught in a PSU on this license may still count toward experience for the salary schedule.
The international faculty license cannot be converted to another license type until it has expired.
The teacher license classifications include the International Faculty License, under LICN-026.

Foreign-educated applicants may fall under the out-of-state applicant rules. The definition of out-of-state applicant includes those who completed a program with a principal place of business outside North Carolina, and expressly includes international preparation programs.

Under the out-of-state rules, an applicant with fewer than three years of licensed experience may qualify for an initial professional license by holding a license in the corresponding area in a jurisdiction outside NC, or by completing an EPP recognized by the jurisdiction where it is based. An applicant with more than three years may qualify for a continuing professional license if the license is clear and the other jurisdiction's requirements are substantially similar, or the applicant holds NBPTS certification.

Initial professional licenses for applicants with out-of-state preparation or licensure are governed by LICN-020, which requires either completion of an NC-recognized EPP, completion of an EPP outside NC, or a clear out-of-state license with fewer than three years of licensed teaching experience there.

answer.summary: The passages show no change to NC license level from National Board certification: license level is set by the highest degree from an educator preparation program. National Board certification does carry renewal benefits: it gives full credit for all eight CEUs in the cycle it is earned, and two CEUs in the cycle it is renewed. Each license issued by DPI includes the applicant's degree level, which is based on the highest degree issued by an educator preparation program. National Board certification is not listed as a factor in this.
An applicant for a professional educator license who holds National Board certification must provide proof of that certification, if applicable, as part of the application.

A teacher who receives National Board Certification receives credit for all eight CEUs for the renewal cycle in which the certification is received. Eight CEUs earned through this credit equals the full eight-CEU requirement for a teacher renewal cycle under LICN-030 §1, so no other CEUs are needed for that cycle.

A teacher who renews a National Board Certification receives credit for two CEUs for the renewal cycle in which the certification is renewed. Two of the eight required CEUs are therefore covered, leaving six CEUs to complete in that cycle (8 − 2 = 6).

For an out-of-state applicant seeking a continuing professional license, holding National Board certification is one of two alternative ways to satisfy the licensing criteria. The other is that the other jurisdiction's requirements are substantially similar to North Carolina's.

The passages do not state that National Board certification changes a teacher's salary-schedule pay level or experience credit. The experience-credit policy (LICN-006) does not mention National Board certification.

Renewal still requires a rating of at least Proficient on three of five standards, including Standard 4, on the most recent annual evaluation for teachers employed by a local board. The passages do not exempt National Board certified teachers from this requirement.

question: How does NC handle licensure for teachers coming from another state?
context_ids: LICN-008 (North Carolina Department of Public Instruction Licensure Fees)

input.query: How does NC handle licensure for teachers coming from another state?
out-of-state applicant three years licensed experience continuing professional license

answer.summary: NC's out-of-state pathway depends mainly on how many years of licensed experience the teacher has. Under three years, the teacher may get an Initial Professional License (IPL), and over three years, a Continuing Professional License (CPL) may be available if the out-of-state license is clear and the other state's requirements are substantially similar to NC's or the teacher holds NBPTS certification. Servicemembers and spouses have a separate recognition route.

claims.text: An out-of-state applicant is defined as anyone who completed an educator or administrator preparation program with a principal place of business outside North Carolina, including international programs.

An out-of-state applicant with fewer than three years of licensed professional educator experience may qualify for an IPL by either holding a license in the corresponding license area in another jurisdiction, or by completing an EPP recognized by the jurisdiction where that EPP has its principal place of business.

For an IPL in Elementary Education or Special Education: General Curriculum, the applicant must meet the applicable NC licensure exam requirements by the end of the third year of licensure, even if they passed an out-of-state exam in that area.

For an IPL in any other license area, the applicant must either pass an out-of-state exam for that area in the examining jurisdiction, or satisfy the applicable NC exam requirements before or during the third year of licensure, having attempted them at least once during the first year.

An out-of-state applicant with more than three years of licensed professional educator experience may qualify for a CPL if they meet both of the following: a clear license from another jurisdiction, and either NBPTS certification or licensure requirements in that jurisdiction that are substantially similar to NC's.

A 'clear license' must be in good standing, renewable by the issuing authority, not revoked or subject to discipline, free of pending unprofessional-conduct investigations, and not voluntarily surrendered during an investigation.
'Substantially similar' means the other jurisdiction required, at minimum, completion of a recognized EPP and a passing score on an out-of-state exam for each license area sought.
Evidence of out-of-state exam results must be presented at initial NC licensure, and an out-of-state applicant may not use those results to convert an IPL to a CPL.

An out-of-state applicant who qualifies for a teacher license may add a teaching area based solely on an out-of-state exam pass, if evidence is submitted at initial application. Adding an area after the NC license is issued falls under LICN-013.

An applicant who completed an EPP outside NC is eligible for an IPL under LICN-020 §1(b). An applicant who holds a clear out-of-state license and has fewer than three years of licensed teaching experience there is eligible under LICN-020 §1(c).

To move from IPL to CPL, a teacher must hold an NC IPL or residency license, satisfy exam requirements before or during the third year of licensure, have at least three years of licensed teaching experience, and complete a Beginning Teacher Support Program unless they have at least three years of licensed teaching experience outside NC.

A servicemember or spouse holding a covered license in another state who relocates to NC on military orders has that license recognized for its covered areas, after submitting proof of orders, a marriage certificate if applicable, and a notarized affidavit.

NC recognizes the out-of-state license until the military orders expire or June 30 of the fiscal year in which they expire, whichever is later. After that, the servicemember or spouse must apply for an NC license under SBE policy to keep working.
For servicemembers and spouses, out-of-state exam scores need not come from the jurisdiction where the EPP was completed.

The out-of-state application fee is $100 for an in-state-style initial professional license opened by an individual educator, per the fee table. This table reflects fees effective January 1, 2017, and the policy is dated 2018-04-05, so the current fee should be confirmed.

For out-of-state applicants, an IPL is available with fewer than three years of licensed professional educator experience. For salary experience credit, one year is earned for full-time work of at least six calendar months within one fiscal year (July 1 through June 30). Part-time work requires at least 15 hours per week, and partial years may be combined. For example, six months of full-time experience equals one year of salary experience credit.

Service as a tutor, clerical paraprofessional, or substitute teacher is not recognized for professional educator experience credit, and time on leave of absence is not credited, except as required by workers' compensation or USERRA.

answer.summary: A residency license (RL) renews under LICN-019 §2 only if the employing PSU documents that the teacher is enrolled in a recognized educator preparation program, is employed as a teacher there, had at least six months of teaching experience in the preceding school year, and completed the first-year professional development. claims.text: A residency license is a one-year license, renewable twice, issued to an individual who meets the qualifications of LICN-019.

The 10 days of professional development may be provided entirely in the preservice period, or as five preservice days with the remaining five taking place during the first year on the residency license.

If the applicant fails to renew a residency license for the second or third year, the license expires. The PSU may ask DPI to reinstate it if the employer hires the applicant within three years of the initial residency license's effective date, the license has not already been renewed twice, and the employer documents current employment and enrollment in a recognized educator preparation program.

The policies provided list the biology degree and the number of hours of coursework only as eligibility factors for the initial residency license (24 hours of content coursework or passing the licensure exam). They do not list a degree or coursework requirement for renewal.

question: Candidate has 5 years of public school teaching in Tennessee and wants a NC Continuing Professional License. Which path applies and what do they still need?

answer.summary: With 5 years of licensed teaching in Tennessee, the candidate is past the three-year threshold for a direct out-of-state CPL under LICN-025 §2, rather than the IPL path. Eligibility then depends on whether the Tennessee license is clear, whether the candidate holds National Board certification or meets the substantially-similar test (EPP plus passing out-of-state exam scores for each license area sought), and the candidate's grade band and current employment, none of which were provided.

claims.text: An out-of-state applicant with more than three years of licensed professional educator experience may qualify for a continuing professional license. The candidate's 5 years exceeds the three-year threshold, so the CPL route in LICN-025 §2 is the one that applies, not the IPL route in LICN-025 §1(a), which covers applicants with fewer than three years.

To qualify for an out-of-state CPL, the applicant must meet both criterion (a), holding a clear license from another jurisdiction, and criterion (b), holding NBPTS certification or having licensure requirements substantially similar to North Carolina's.

A clear license must be in good standing, renewable by the issuing authority, not revoked or disciplined, free of any pending unprofessional-conduct investigation in any state, and not voluntarily surrendered while under investigation. The candidate's Tennessee license must be checked against each of these conditions.

Under the substantially-similar route, the other jurisdiction must have required completion of an educator preparation program recognized by the state where the EPP is located, and a passing score on an out-of-state exam for each license area for which NC licensure is sought.
If the candidate holds National Board for Professional Teaching Standards certification, criterion (b) is met without the EPP and exam test, so the exam question does not arise on that route.

For an out-of-state CPL based on exam results, the applicant must present evidence of the exam results at the time of initial licensure in North Carolina. Exam results cannot be used to convert an IPL to a CPL.

A CPL based on a clear out-of-state license must meet LICN-025. The passages do not say whether the Beginning Teacher Support Program requirement in LICN-024 §1(d) applies to this route; LICN-024 §1(d)(i) exempts applicants with at least three years of licensed teaching experience outside North Carolina, which the candidate appears to meet, but the passages do not confirm that this exemption governs the LICN-024 §3 route.

Once issued, a CPL is renewed every five years. Teachers in Grades 6-12 must complete eight CEUs per cycle: four in the license area and four general CEUs. Teachers in Pre-K through Grade 5 must complete eight CEUs: three in license area, three literacy, and two general. Teachers employed by a local board must also have a rating of at least proficient on their most recent annual evaluation, including proficient on Standard 4.

Under LICN-025 §4, if the candidate later wants to add a license area, they must rely on an out-of-state exam passed in that area, submitted with the initial application, or follow LICN-013 after licensure.

claims.text: The lateral entry license under G.S. 115C-297 was repealed by S.L. 2017-189, so it is no longer an available pathway under current policy. The passages mention it only as a historical reference for people who held it earlier.

The Pre-School add-on cannot be issued as a standalone license. It can be added only to an existing Elementary Education, Special Education, or Family and Consumer Sciences – General license, so a preschool background alone does not create a Birth-K license.

A limited license is available only to someone who previously held a lateral entry license under G.S. 115C-297 and meets the other stated conditions. It is not available to this applicant unless that prior license is confirmed.

To renew a limited license, the licensee must meet or exceed expected growth as measured by EVAAS, where such data is available. If more than one year of growth data exists, DPI averages it.
